text:
Priya Rao: Quick thread to align on private-deploy roadmap items for next cycle. I want clear owners + smallest shippable increments for: airgap packaging, upgrade safety, and customer-managed networking.
Evan Brooks: 👍 agree. propose we aim for a pilotable "airgap bundle v1" that includes: signed images, bundled deps, and a verification checksum manifest. minimal engineering to get customers fully offline.
Tina Morales: For upgrades, let's not aim for full rolling across all topologies in one go. MVP: sequential node upgrades with a canary on a non-prod tenant and a manual promotable cutover. automation later.
Samir Iqbal: Networking is the recurring pain. Two modes: "managed-peering" (we orchestrate peering) vs "customer-managed" (they handle BGP/IPAM). MVP should support customer-managed via documented hooks + validation, not orchestration.
Jordan Lee: For the airgap bundle, also include dependency mirroring instructions and a small local registry helper script. Example:
```
# mirror images
skopeo copy docker://ghcr.io/redwood/agent:latest dir:/tmp/airgap/agent
```
That reduces hand-holding.
Priya Rao: Good. Also require bundle signing: cosign signatures to prove provenance. Customers asked explicitly.
Evan Brooks: Acceptance criteria proposal for Packaging (airgap v1):
- bundle can be consumed by offline installer without external DNS
- cosign verified signatures for all images
- install completes within 20 mins on 4 CPU/16GB VM
- clear error codes for missing deps
I'll draft a short checklist.
Tina Morales: Upgrades acceptance criteria (MVP):
- single-node upgrade with health checks before proceeding
- explicit rollback artifact pinned (image + manifest)
- canary tenant traffic validated for 15 min window
- operator will not auto-promote without manual approval
Samir Iqbal: Networking checklist (customer-managed mode):
- validated customer CIDR non-overlap check
- documented recommended NAT strategy + floating IP example
- port/proto matrix (22, 443, 9411 tcp; 53 udp for DNS)
- a tiny connectivity test script that runs from their network to verify routes
Jordan Lee: Add a short CLI sample for ip-preserve check:
```
# check for preserved NAT mapping
curl -sS http://metadata.internal/wan-ip || echo "no metadata"
```
This helps field engineers.
Priya Rao: Policy question: should auto-upgrade be opt-in or opt-out? legal prefers explicit opt-in. I'd prefer opt-in with an enterprise contract clause.
Evan Brooks: Opt-in only. We need a feature flag plus UI checkbox. Also telemetry opt-in so we can collect post-upgrade metrics for regressions.
Tina Morales: Pilot candidate: NimbusCorp (large onprem, strict firewall rules). If they sign, we test airgap + customer-managed networking flow. We should scope Windows support out of pilot.
Samir Iqbal: Implementation note: for customer-managed BGP we need to provide clear AS-path expectations and a sample BGP config snippet — add that to docs.
ci-bot: pipeline/airgap-bundle:v1 succeeded for tag: pilot-1737012345
Jordan Lee: Can we add a short risk log in the playbook? Major risks: kernel compatibility, DNS/TLS chain issues in airgap, and operator-image rollback complexity.
Priya Rao: Action items:
- Evan: airgap bundle checklist + cosign howto (due Wed)
- Tina: upgrade runbook + rollback template (due Wed)
- Samir: networking validation scripts + BGP snippet (due Wed)
- Jordan: playbook risk log + pilot run plan for NimbusCorp (due Thu)
I'll collate into the public PM sync doc on Thu afternoon.
Evan Brooks: I'll include a minimal troubleshooting table for common install failures.
Tina Morales: I'll add the canary metrics we want to surface (p50/p95 latency, error-rate, cpu pressure).
Samir Iqbal: Noted. Also flag legal/contract for auto-upgrade opt-in.
Priya Rao: Thanks all. Keeping thread for the record. We'll use this content in the quarterly roadmap board.
